messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 80
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Social Worker
  trauma_type: Physical abuse by romantic partner
  pcl5: 66

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Male Presence: Being alone with men, Known People: Related people, Auditory (Door): Doors opening or slamming
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Dreams: Situations or times of day that tend to bring on nightmares, Memory Erasure: I try to erase the memory of the event, Meaning Seeking: I think about why the event has happened to me
  Threat: Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep, Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: Confused Sequence: I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order, Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind., Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
  Negative Appraisals: Shattered Beliefs: My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed, Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened, Mistrust: People can't be trusted

Vignette:
Giovanna had always prided herself on her strength and independence. As a social worker, she spent decades helping others navigate their darkest moments, but it was her own life that would eventually become marked by trauma. It started with the man she thought loved her - her partner of several years who, behind closed doors, turned out to be capable of unimaginable cruelty. One particular night still seared itself into her memory like a branding iron: the sound of the door slamming open as he stormed in, his face twisted in rage. The sequence of events that followed was hazy, but snapshots of the terror she felt remained etched in vivid detail - the feeling of being trapped, the helplessness, and the pain. The aftermath of that night was a blur of fear and confusion. Giovanna found herself avoiding situations that brought back those memories, like being alone with men or encountering people related to her ex-partner. Even the sound of doors opening or slamming sent her heart racing. She tried to erase the memory of the event from her mind, hoping it would somehow diminish its power over her. But as time went on, Giovanna began to question why this had happened to her - a search for meaning that provided no answers but plenty of sleepless nights. Her normally sharp mind now felt clouded by hypervigilance; she constantly scanned for exits whenever she entered a new room or building, always on the lookout for potential threats. Her belief in the goodness of people was shattered, and she couldn't help but feel dirty, contaminated by what had been done to her. Mistrust crept into every relationship, making it impossible for her to form connections with others. As a social worker, Giovanna's occupation required empathy and understanding - qualities that now felt like liabilities. Her work began to suffer as she struggled to connect with clients who reminded her of her ex-partner or the traumatic event itself. She started avoiding certain cases or situations at work, not wanting to trigger those memories again. The consequences were immediate; her relationships with colleagues became strained, and her performance was called into question. Despite her best efforts to move on, Giovanna's grief over what had happened still felt overwhelming whenever she recalled that night. She couldn't put the memories in order - it was as if time itself had been distorted by the trauma. Her mind replayed those snapshots of fear and pain like a broken record, tormenting her. It wasn't until Giovanna found herself unable to sleep for weeks on end, her hypervigilance making even her own home feel unsafe, that she realized she needed help. The physical toll of her symptoms was evident - dark circles under her eyes, weight loss, and an exhaustion that went beyond mere fatigue. Her fear wasn't just about what had happened; it was about losing herself to the trauma, becoming a shadow of the strong, independent woman she once was. As Giovanna sat in her therapist's office for the first time, she knew she was taking the first tentative steps towards reclaiming her life. She was scared - scared of reliving those memories, scared of facing the pain and grief that still lingered. But most of all, she was scared of never being able to heal, of being forever trapped in this cycle of fear and mistrust. Giovanna's journey ahead would be long and arduous, but with each step, she hoped to rebuild not just her sense of self but also her shattered beliefs about the world - a world that once seemed so full of promise and now felt fraught with danger.
